title: Fire, smoke or a burn

differential.label: Smoke inhalation. Emergency
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Signs can be delayed for up to 2 hours.

differential.label: Carbon monoxide poisoning. Emergency
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. A small fire can make a lot of carbon monoxide. The oximeter can read falsely normal.

differential.label: Minor burn: red skin, pain, smaller than the palm
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis.

differential.label: Deep or large burn: blisters, white or charred skin, or larger than the palm
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Needs flight surgeon review now.

differential.label: Electrical burn. Emergency
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Can hurt the heart and organs even when the skin looks fine.

tests.title: Pulse
tests.instruction: Read the pulse. Enter it. Repeat every 5 minutes.

tests.title: Blood pressure, top number
tests.instruction: Take the blood pressure. Enter the top number. Repeat every 5 minutes.

tests.title: Oxygen level
tests.instruction: Clip the pulse oximeter on a finger. Enter the oxygen level. Do not trust a normal number after smoke.

tests.title: Breathing rate
tests.instruction: Count breaths for 1 minute. Write down the number.

tests.title: Burn size
tests.instruction: Count how many of the person’s own palms would cover the burn. Write down the number.

tests.title: Pain score
tests.instruction: Enter a pain score from 0 to 10.

immediateSteps.title: Fire or smoke: put on your mask first
immediateSteps.instruction: Put on a protective mask now. Do not wait for air readings. Follow the station fire procedure.

immediateSteps.title: Get the person out of the smoke
immediateSteps.instruction: Move the person out of the affected module with the crew. Close the hatch as the fire procedure says. Keep a mask on the person.

immediateSteps.title: If they are not breathing, start CPR
immediateSteps.instruction: Check breathing and pulse. If there is none, start CPR now.

immediateSteps.title: Check the airway
immediateSteps.instruction: Look for soot around the mouth. Look for singed nose hair. Listen for noisy breathing.

immediateSteps.title: Take vital signs every 5 minutes
immediateSteps.instruction: Enter pulse, blood pressure and oxygen level. Count breaths. Repeat every 5 minutes.

immediateSteps.title: Do not trust a normal oxygen reading
immediateSteps.instruction: Treat the person as poisoned after smoke even if the oxygen level looks normal.

immediateSteps.title: Electrical burn: cut the power first
immediateSteps.instruction: Do not touch the person until the power is off. Then check pulse and breathing.

immediateSteps.title: Cool the burn
immediateSteps.instruction: Cool the burn with a wet gauze pad, a wet towel or a drink bag. Do not use ice.

immediateSteps.title: Leave stuck clothing and blisters
immediateSteps.instruction: Do not pull off clothing stuck to the burn. Do not break blisters.

immediateSteps.title: Cover the burn
immediateSteps.instruction: Cover the burn with a clean, dry dressing. Tape it loosely.

immediateSteps.title: Estimate burn size
immediateSteps.instruction: Use the person’s palm as about 1 percent of the body. Enter how many palms the burn covers.

immediateSteps.title: Send the case to the flight surgeon
immediateSteps.instruction: Continue to handoff and send the case. Keep watching for 2 hours after smoke.

cautions: This card is not a diagnosis. It gives no doses. The station fire procedure comes first; this card does not replace it. Put on your own mask before you help. Carbon monoxide can make the oximeter read falsely normal. Do not put ice, creams or ointments on a severe burn. Use any kit item only as the flight surgeon directs.
sourceNote: Researcher card, Pulseframe Batch 2, 2026-11-15. Built from NASA IMM data, OCHMO-TB-008 Fire Protection, the 2001 ISS medical checklist (historical), the NASA Human Research Roadmap smoke inhalation page and MedlinePlus first aid. Not a current NASA procedure. Pending second-person safety review.
redFlagsLifeThreat: Trouble breathing, noisy breathing or wheezing.
Soot around the mouth or singed nose hair.
Confusion or any change in mental state.
Burn larger than the palm, or white or charred skin.
redFlagsCallGround: Anyone who breathed smoke, even if they feel fine.
A minor burn that still hurts after 48 hours.

timeLimits.item: Put on masks at once. Do not wait for air readings.
Signs of smoke poisoning can be delayed for up to 2 hours. Keep watching for at least that long.
Airway injury symptoms usually start within minutes but can take up to 24 hours.
Earth advice for minor burns is to cool for at least 5 to 30 minutes. No source gives a cooling time for the in-flight wet cloth method.
A minor burn that still hurts after 48 hours needs the flight surgeon.

whenGroundUnavailable.status: PARTIAL (historical rule found, no current rule)
whenGroundUnavailable.detail: The 2001 ISS burns procedure says that in an emergency or during loss of signal the crew begins treatment, then calls the surgeon as soon as possible. No current public rule was found. Looked in: OCHMO-TB-008, OCHMO-TB-044, 2001 ISS checklist, HRR smoke inhalation page.
firstAidThatNeedsNoGround: Masks on, move out of the smoke, close the hatch per the fire procedure.
Vital signs every 5 minutes, written down with the time.
Send the case as soon as the link returns.

Already proposed in new-measurement-keys.csv. No SpCO device was found in equipment.json, so this stays unused for now.

proposedKeys.unit: count of palms (about 1 percent body surface each)
proposedKeys.reason: Appended to new-measurement-keys.csv (2026-11-15). Lets the app flag a burn larger than the palm. Not in keys.ts yet.

candidateItemNotes: Acetaminophen and ibuprofen are in inventory.json; MedlinePlus says they can relieve burn pain. Bacitracin is listed for minor skin wounds; MedlinePlus mentions an antibiotic lotion for minor burns once cooled, and says no ointment on severe burns. Burn bandage, nonstick bandage, rolled gauze and the 2001 burn creams are in NASA kit lists but not in inventory.json. equipmentIds lists equipment.json ids used by the tests and steps.
gaps: No source gives a cooling time for burns in flight, or says how to keep cooling water from floating free beyond a wet cloth.
No SpCO (carbon monoxide) meter found in equipment.json, yet the oximeter is unreliable after smoke.
Burn dressings are not in inventory.json.
IMM burn and smoke rates are model-derived from ISS fire estimates, not flight cases.
The current ISS smoke and burn procedures are not public; the 2001 version is used.
